patient_information: A 24-year-old single woman from the highlands of Peru, with no children, who was previously healthy.
chief_complaint: Upper abdominal pain, weight loss (5 kg), nausea, vomiting, and intermittent fevers.
history_of_present_illness: For 2 months, the patient experienced upper abdominal pain, weight loss, nausea, and vomiting, along with intermittent fevers for the past 2 weeks, which did not respond to analgesics. Three days prior, an abdominal ultrasound showed multiple hypoechoic liver lesions, leading to initial treatment with ceftriaxone and metronidazole for suspected pyogenic liver abscesses, without improvement.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Patient is from the Peruvian Andes and started taking over-the-counter medicines to lose weight, changed her diet to vegetarian food, and consumed energetic hot drinks made from alfalfa and watercress 2 to 3 months ago.
physical_exam: Patient looks ill with pale mucous membranes, no jaundice. Abdomen has right upper quadrant tenderness, and the liver is slightly enlarged with a span of 15 cm. The rest of the physical examination is normal.
labs_and_diagnostics: Blood tests revealed WBC 13.94 x 10^9/L, Eosinophils 43% (total 5.97), Haemoglobin 12.3 g/dL, AST 34 U/L, ALT 55 U/L, AP 170 U/L, Amylase 75 U/L, Lipase 100 U/L. A contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen showed multiple hypodense, non-enhancing lesions in the liver. Fas2 ELISA titre was 0.56 (normal <0.2).
differential_diagnosis: Suspected pyogenic liver abscesses, fascioliasis, amoebic liver abscess, brucellosis, visceral toxocariasis, ascariasis, and hydatid disease.
management_and_clinical_course: Initially treated with ceftriaxone and metronidazole without improvement. Following a Fas2 ELISA diagnosis, the patient received a single dose of triclabendazole 10 mg/kg, after which her clinical symptoms rapidly improved, laboratory parameters normalized, and liver lesions disappeared on control tomography.
